target_profile.system_boundary: Captured Go raft module, including RawNode/Node APIs, raft core, log/storage, progress/quorum and configuration packages. Host transport, durable medium and application are caller responsibilities; in-repository adapters remain to be traced.

behaviors.protocol_context: Leader term and current voter configuration
behaviors.trigger: Accepted MsgAppResp or switchToConfig calls maybeCommit
reads: Peer Match indexes, voter sets, current term, local log term at quorum index
important_branches: maybeCommit advances only beyond previous committed index at a nonzero matching current term.
MsgAppResp success that updates progress and advances commitment invokes releasePendingReadIndexMessages and bcastAppend.
switchToConfig advancing commitment calls bcastAppend without invoking releasePendingReadIndexMessages.
unknowns: Whether another guaranteed trigger releases previously queued reads when switchToConfig supplies the first current-term commit.

behaviors.execution_owner: raft Step, campaign, role transition methods
behaviors.trigger: Election campaign, higher-term message, or role transition
reads: Message term and type, lease interval, local vote, last log identity
writes: Term, Vote, role, leader, progress, readOnly state
important_branches: reset preserves Vote within a term and clears it on term change; resets progress and readOnly but not the committed log prefix.
Pre-candidate transition does not increment term or reset Vote.
Lower-term ordinary responses return before role-specific consumption. Lower-term storage append responses do not stabilize entries but may acknowledge a snapshot.
Actual votes require canVote and an up-to-date candidate log; response publication uses msgsAfterAppend.

Candidate handler only tallies the response type corresponding to real or pre-candidacy. Unique peer votes are evaluated against configured majorities; pre-vote victory starts a real election, actual victory becomes leader and appends a no-op.

Ticks campaign only if promotable and randomized timeout passes; CheckQuorum can step a leader down. Transfer pauses proposals, waits for target Match to reach the log end, sends TimeoutNow and expires after electionTimeout.
Committed but unaccounted configuration entries block hup through hasUnappliedConfChanges; this guard relies on raftLog.applied rather than directly checking completion of ApplyConfChange.

behaviors.protocol_context: Ready batch, synchronous or asynchronous storage mode
writes: Ready messages and storage work; stepsOnAdvance; accepted unstable/application work
important_branches: Synchronous Ready.Messages includes deferred peer replies and explicitly requires Entries persistence before send. Self replies run through Advance.

Async storage append messages attach all deferred replies and a term-stamped stabilization response. Even an empty append can carry prior-state-dependent replies. Same-target reliable FIFO is a caller duty.
Async stabilization uses both current response term and entry identity; lower-term responses cannot remove unstable entries, while snapshot completion remains term-independent.
Node serializes core calls and prevents another synchronous Ready until Advance; both Node and RawNode reject unexpected network local messages and unknown-peer responses.
async_boundaries: Host persists entries, HardState and snapshots; external storage completion is not established by Ready emission.
Async mode issues local storage messages; synchronous mode places self-responses into stepsOnAdvance and publishes non-self deferred responses in Ready.Messages.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Append acknowledgments are queued behind persistence by send; leader self-ack is also deferred.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Vote responses are queued behind persistence before becoming usable election support.

behaviors.protocol_context: Committed Ready batch or local apply message
behaviors.trigger: Ready acceptance schedules work; Advance or MsgStorageApplyResp accounts for completion
writes: applying, applied, outstanding application bytes and proposal accounting
important_branches: Synchronous Advance steps the apply response captured at Ready acceptance regardless of whether ApplyConfChange was called. Node contract explicitly permits Advance while application is ongoing.

Async Ready does not permit unstable committed entries to be applied; outstanding snapshots block entry application. Async apply responses are delivered after work completion and are term-independent.
appliedTo can propose automatic joint exit when leader and applied frontier passes pendingConfIndex; configuration application alone does not call appliedTo.

Automatic joint exit is attempted in appliedTo when AutoLeave, applied >= pendingConfIndex and StateLeader hold. A concurrent leadership transfer causes Step(MsgProp) to drop this request. abortLeaderTransfer only clears leadTransferee; heartbeat ticks do not directly retry automatic exit.

cross_activity_effects.A2: The accounted applied frontier bounds the scan used to forbid campaigns with unapplied committed configuration changes. A pending leadership transfer also suppresses the automatic-exit proposal generated on application acknowledgment.
cross_activity_effects.A4: Host calls ApplyConfChange on consumed configuration entries; application acknowledgment also triggers automatic joint exit.

unknowns: Whether early synchronous Advance is permitted before ApplyConfChange, or whether the configuration callback has a stricter completion boundary.
Whether a failed transfer after suppressing automatic exit has another retry trigger when no further entries are proposed or applied.

behaviors.protocol_context: Applied configuration entry and current incoming/outgoing voters
important_branches: Simple changes cannot alter more than one voter or run inside joint state; zero voters are rejected.
EnterJoint preserves the old voters as outgoing; LeaveJoint drops outgoing voters and activates staged learners. Retained peers retain progress; new peers start Match zero.
Leader admission ordinarily allows at most one unapplied configuration proposal; invalid requests become empty normal entries.
switchToConfig updates eligibility and may recompute commitment; removal/demotion steps down only when configured, and removed leaders cannot propose new entries.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Changes which Match values count toward commitment and which votes count toward decisions.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Changes campaign/transfer eligibility and leader-removal behavior.

behaviors.execution_owner: raft append/snapshot handlers and progress replication
behaviors.protocol_context: Follower log prefix and leader progress
behaviors.trigger: MsgApp, MsgSnap, rejections, heartbeat recovery and transport reports
important_branches: Follower matches previous entry identity, truncates only conflicting uncommitted suffix, and caps propagated commit by received log end. Heartbeat commit is capped at peer Match by sender.
Rejections adjust Next; heartbeat responses can unpause and send empty appends after lost in-flight messages. Missing local history triggers snapshot fetch if peer recently active.
Snapshot restore ignores obsolete indexes, refuses a recipient absent from membership, fast-forwards matching log history, otherwise restores log and configuration.
Snapshot failure and unreachable reports return progress to probing; successful snapshot or append acknowledgments resume replication.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Repairs eligible durable support while guarding established committed prefixes.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Snapshot acceptance is on follower paths; pending snapshots prevent campaigning.

important_branches: Storage supplies HardState and snapshot ConfState; log starts at compacted prefix, HardState loads bounded commit/term/vote, optional Config.Applied sets replay boundary, then node becomes follower.
ConfState reconstruction creates outgoing configuration before joint incoming changes, preserving learner staging.
MemoryStorage is an in-repository implementation with append suffix replacement, snapshots and compaction; actual crash durability is external.
Bootstrap installs initial committed configuration entries and membership but leaves application frontier behind so host consumes them.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Restart retains committed prefix and log evidence but reconstructs volatile progress.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Persistent term/vote survive restart; node does not resume as leader.

behaviors.execution_owner: Leader/follower ReadIndex handlers and host read consumer
behaviors.protocol_context: Request context, current term, committed index and read mode
behaviors.trigger: ReadIndex, current-term commit release, heartbeat acknowledgments or forwarded result
important_branches: Non-singleton leader postpones requests until an entry is committed in its term. The singleton shortcut checks only that incoming voter count is one and outgoing count is zero, then returns the local committed index; it does not itself verify that the sole voter is the requesting leader.
Safe mode records request/index, self-acknowledges and broadcasts a context heartbeat; current configured quorum acknowledgments advance the queue and produce local ReadStates or remote responses.
Lease mode returns the committed index after its admission condition. Host must correlate context and wait for state-machine application before serving reads.
Role reset clears readOnly quorum acknowledgments; pending pre-first-commit requests survive reset and may later be released with a fresh index/quorum. API allows lost requests and requires retries.

When a fully applied demotion leaves the local node as learner and another node as the sole voter, StepDownOnRemoval=false permits StateLeader to remain. Its singleton ReadIndex branch returns the local committed index without a voter-confirmation round; cardinality alone does not establish local voter authority.
unknowns: Reachability of first current-term commit via switchToConfig without release; an unexecuted path alone does not establish a liveness violation.

facts.meaning: The leader commit boundary has advanced to a log index whose term matches its current term, based on current voter Match aggregation. This alone does not establish that pending reads were released or entries were applied.
facts.validity_context: Leader-side maybeCommit with current tracker configuration. The committed prefix survives role changes, while the assertion that its term equals the current term must be reevaluated after a term change.
facts.durability: In-memory commit advancement; host persistence and application completion are separate.
facts.recovery: newRaft restores persisted committed history from HardState and snapshot; the current-term condition is recomputed rather than restored as a separate flag.

facts.meaning: raftLog.applied is the monotonic frontier accounted as applied by raft after startup initialization, snapshot acknowledgment, or application acknowledgment. In synchronous mode the acknowledgment is generated by Advance; actual host completion depends on caller ordering and is not independently observed.
facts.validity_context: Committed prefix of this instance; term-independent. Ready acceptance advances applying separately. Node permits synchronous Advance while commands are still being applied, so this field alone cannot attest external completion.
facts.durability: Volatile accounting; caller supplies Applied on restart and maintains state machine/snapshot durability.
facts.recovery: Initialized to compacted prefix, optionally Config.Applied; snapshot acknowledgment can advance it.
unknowns: Whether configuration installation must precede early Advance even though ordinary application may overlap.

facts.meaning: The local tracker records the installed incoming/outgoing voter sets and learner eligibility. Singleton cardinality does not by itself establish that the local node belongs to that voting set.

identity.configuration: Installed tracker voter and learner sets

facts.validity_context: Established by applying configuration changes or restoring ConfState. Leader role can persist when local membership changes if StepDownOnRemoval is false.
facts.durability: Volatile tracker configuration; caller records returned ConfState in snapshots and replays committed changes.
facts.recovery: confchange.Restore recreates voter sets and learner staging from ConfState.

surfaces.reason: Unlike MsgAppResp commitment advancement, configuration-driven advancement does not directly release pending ReadIndex messages. Determine a legal history and alternative release triggers before attributing a wakeup duty.

Ready.Entries and Ready.Messages explicitly require persistence before synchronous sends; rawnode agrees. doc.go still permits same-batch overlap. Preserve this documentation conflict; the looser order cannot be presumed legal for implementation attribution.

Node permits early Advance while application is ongoing, but campaign admission scans only above the accounted applied frontier. Determine whether configuration installation must precede Advance and whether stale eligibility can reach a campaign.

surfaces.entry_point: stepLeader MsgReadIndex -> ProgressTracker.IsSingleton after leader removal
surfaces.reason: The source path permits a retained demoted StateLeader to return a local read result when a different node is sole voter. Any wider client endpoint consequence remains separate from the local eligibility requirement.

surfaces.entry_point: raft.appliedTo automatic exit -> transfer suppression -> abortLeaderTransfer
surfaces.reason: Automatic exit may be dropped during transfer. Determine whether timeout provides another trigger without requiring a fresh external proposal, and which bounded progress duty applies.

formation.explanation: Leader proposals receive term/index, append to the log and queue a persistence-delayed self acknowledgment. Peer acknowledgments update progress; tracker aggregates current voters using both majorities for joint configuration, then maybeCommit checks the current log term before advancing commitment. Acknowledgment-driven advancement broadcasts append and releases queued reads, while configuration-driven advancement broadcasts without that release. Voter sets use n/2+1 majorities. Followers match the preceding entry, protect committed history and publish durable append responses. Rejection probes, heartbeat recovery and snapshots replenish lagging support. Ready delivers committed entries separately from actual host application.

context.explanation: Campaign transitions establish candidate term and self vote; vote eligibility uses local vote/leader context and log freshness. PreVote leaves term and vote unchanged. Step handles message terms before role handlers, with explicit pre-vote/lease exceptions and lower-term rejection. Role reset clears accumulated progress and readOnly context while preserving the committed prefix. Candidate handlers accept the matching vote response kind, deduplicate votes and tally current voters. Pre-vote success starts an actual campaign; real quorum success elects a leader and appends its no-op. Timer quorum loss and higher terms revoke leadership; transfer waits for target replication and expires. Campaign admission excludes learners, pending snapshots and committed configuration entries above the accounted applied frontier.

connection.explanation: Term dispatch prevents ordinary old responses from becoming new leader support. Persistence-delayed vote/append replies and leader self replies connect durable support to election and commit decisions. Configuration application reinterprets peer progress through a changed voter set and may itself advance commitment; established committed history constrains snapshots and subsequent log repair. Host configuration installation changes voter eligibility separately from application accounting. Restart restores term/vote, committed history and ConfState, while volatile support is rebuilt. Async storage uses FIFO completion and term-stamped append responses; application acknowledgments remain term-independent. Old pre-first-commit read requests can survive a reset, but read quorum acknowledgments do not; any later release uses current committed state and a fresh read round. Synchronous early Advance can account application before external completion, leaving configuration admission timing as a focused unresolved premise. A demoted StateLeader can satisfy the cardinality-only singleton read branch without being the voter when step-down is disabled; this is a local authority-consumption gap distinct from early application accounting.

open_details: Pending-read release following configuration-driven first current-term commit.
Synchronous persistence/send ordering discrepancy across interface descriptions.
Whether early synchronous Advance may precede configuration installation and allow campaigning with stale membership.
Flow-control limits, all snapshot overlap histories and optional lease clock assumptions are not exhaustively investigated.
Automatic joint-exit scheduling after a leadership transfer suppresses the application-triggered proposal and later times out.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation, authority, old-work, configuration, persistence, recovery and consumption paths are now traced. Local contract and scheduling uncertainties remain explicit and do not prevent focused investigation.
